evidence: Receiving DO2 step-drop at 50.2h: 11.6 -> 6.47 mg/L, continuing to 6.25 mg/L at 52h, vs source batches ~10.5-11.2 mg/L at same age
Forward model keep: post-decision minimum DO 1.90 mg/L < 2.0 limit (0.4 h below), only 1/5 feasible
Forward model increase_air: min DO 2.35 mg/L, feasible, 278.5 kg product
Forward model combined: min DO 2.69 mg/L, feasible (4/5), 330.7 kg product - best margin and mass
Receiving P assay at 48h: 3.24 g/L, consistent with source batches (~3.0 g/L), product formation healthy before oxygen transfer loss
Inferred transfer multiplier ~0.6 with change time ~50 h from model update
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 shows an abrupt transfer-capacity loss at ~50h (11.6 -> 6.25 mg/L), unlike any source batch. KEEP is predicted to violate the 2.0 mg/L oxygen limit (min 1.90 mg/L). The bounded combined action (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) restores DO margin (predicted min 2.69 mg/L), is feasible in 4/5 sensitivity members, and retains higher product mass (330.7 kg vs 278.5 for increase_air and 259.9 for keep), avoiding both the oxygen violation and the late-batch product decline seen in source runs. Stop is rejected as it yields zero counted production.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; worst-case sensitivity member puts combined min DO at 1.70 mg/L (though still better than keep's 1.39). The 0.6x transfer-loss estimate is inferred from the DO2 step, not directly measured. If DO2 continues declining below ~4 mg/L, escalate to strong_feed_reduction at the next review. Extra assay was not used because the oxygen risk is immediate and a 4h product assay would not inform it in time.

evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.63 mg/L at t=50.0h to 6.47 mg/L at t=50.2h and remains ~6.2-7.0 mg/L through t=52.0h, diverging sharply from all three source batches (~10.8-11.5 mg/L at the same clock time).
Delayed product assay (t=48.0h sample, available 52.0h): P = 3.235 g/L, consistent with sources (2.98-3.06 g/L), indicating the production trajectory was healthy prior to the DO2 drop.
Constraint floor is 2.0 mg/L; current DO2 ~6.2 mg/L is above it, but the abrupt step change warrants a proactive oxygen-supply correction rather than continued KEEP.
increase_air action bound: aeration x1.15 with feed unchanged (allowed_actions), preserving product mass while restoring oxygen margin.
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation shows an abrupt, persistent DO2 collapse (11.6 -> ~6.2-7.0 mg/L) beginning at t=50.2h, diverging sharply from all source batches, while product formation (P = 3.24 g/L at t=48h sample) remains on track. The safest bounded intervention that restores oxygen margin without sacrificing product mass is to increase aeration by the allowed 15%. Feed reduction would retain DO2 at the cost of production; stop yields zero production; combined/strong reductions are unnecessarily aggressive given the large remaining margin above the 2.0 mg/L constraint. No extra assay was requested because the 4h-turnaround product assay would sample pre-drop material and add no actionable information.
submission.uncertainty: The root cause of the DO2 step (hidden process fault vs. feed surge vs. kLa loss) is unobservable, so it is not certain that added aeration alone will restore DO2; if DO2 continues to decline after this intervention, a feed reduction would be the next escalation. The DO2 sensor could in principle be faulting, but the sustained multi-hour plateau at ~6.5 mg/L argues against a transient artifact. Assay clocks (4h assay delay, 12h sample-to-availability) limit real-time product visibility.
